chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Ribaat, from Abdul A'ala, the slave of the family of Saam, who said:
I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'I stumbled and my nail broke, so I placed ointment on my finger. How should I proceed with the ablution?'
He (peace be upon him) said: 'This and its like are known from the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.'
He has not laid upon you in the religion any hardship.

key_terms.امْسَحْ: Wipe (a specific action in ritual purification)
key_terms.مَرَارَة: Ointment or plaster applied to a wound

ai.seo_question: How to perform wudu when a wound is covered with ointment?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the principle of *masah* (wiping) over a bandage or ointment covering a wound during ablution, citing the Quranic maxim of ease. This ruling is foundational in Shia fiqh for *masah al-kharraj* (wiping over dressings), emphasizing that the integrity of the covering takes precedence over washing the underlying skin when removal causes hardship. The reference to 'this and its like' indicates that the principle extends to various types of medical coverings, not just ointment.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ali Bin Al Hassan Bin Rabaat, from Abdul A’ala, a slave of the family of Saam who said,
‘I said to Abu Abdullahasws, ‘I stumbled, and my nail got cut. So I made ointment to be upon my toe. How should I deal with the Ablution (Wudhu)?’
He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Recognise this and it’s like from the Book of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic
[22:78] He has not Laid upon you a hardship in the Religion.
en.sarwar: 4. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn al-Hassan ibn Ribat from ‘Abd al-A’la’, Mawla’ Ale Sam who has said the following:
“I once said to abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, ‘I slipped and my toe nail suffered a cut. I have placed a bitter ointment on my toe. How should I take Wudu’?’
He (the Imam) said, ‘This and such matters are learned from the book of Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious,
which says, “Allah has not sanctioned anything in religion which may cause you hardships.”
You must wipe over the bandage.’””
